title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Note 24 Reportable Operating Segments and Geographic Operations (p153): segment composition factors
key_points: 公司在评估报告分部构成时考虑的因素包括：首席运营决策者审阅的业绩、经济特征、提供的产品与服务、客户类别、产品分销渠道、地理考量（主要是美国 vs 美国以外）、以及监管环境考量。
因此「United States versus outside the United States」是分部划分的地理主轴，而非地理运营表的列结构。
raw_excerpt: We consider a combination of factors when evaluating the composition of our reportable operating segments, including the results reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, economic characteristics, products and services offered, classes of customers, product distribution channels, geographic considerations (primarily United States versus outside the United States), and regulatory environment considerations.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Note 24 (p153): 2022 segment realignment into USCS/CS/ICS/GMNS + Corporate & Other
key_points: 自 2022 年第三季度起，为反映 2022 年第二季度宣布的组织架构调整，公司重新划分报告分部；前期金额已重述以符合新分部口径。
四个新报告分部为 U.S. Consumer Services (USCS)、Commercial Services (CS)、International Card Services (ICS)、Global Merchant and Network Services (GMNS)。
公司职能及某些其他业务与运营计入 Corporate & Other。
自 2022 年第一季度起，公司更新了某些收入的分摊方法，前期金额已重述。
raw_excerpt: Effective for the third quarter of 2022, we realigned our reportable segments to reflect organizational changes announced during the second quarter of 2022. Prior periods have been recast to conform to the new reportable operating segments. The following is a brief description of the primary business activities of our four new reportable operating segments: … Corporate functions and certain other businesses and operations are included in Corporate & Other.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Note 24 (p153): USCS segment definition
key_points: USCS 面向美国消费者发行范围广泛的自营消费卡。
USCS 还向美国消费者提供旅行与生活方式服务，以及银行与非卡类融资产品。
raw_excerpt: U.S. Consumer Services (USCS), which issues a wide range of proprietary consumer cards and provides services to U.S. consumers, including travel and lifestyle services as well as banking and non-card financing products.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Table 11 preceding text (p57): Commercial Services segment definition
key_points: CS 面向美国企业发行范围广泛的自营公司卡与小型企业卡，并提供支付与费用管理、银行及非卡类融资产品等服务。
CS 同时向部分全球企业客户（select global corporate clients）发行自营公司卡并提供服务，因此 CS 并非纯美国分部。
raw_excerpt: CS issues a wide range of proprietary corporate and small business cards and provides services to U.S. businesses, including payment and expense management, banking and non-card financing products. CS also issues proprietary corporate cards and provides services to select global corporate clients.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Table 13 preceding text (p60): International Card Services segment definition
key_points: ICS 在美国以外发行范围广泛的自营消费卡、小企业卡与公司卡。
ICS 为国际客户提供服务，包括旅行与生活方式服务。
ICS 管理部分国际合资企业（international joint ventures）及公司的忠诚度联盟业务（loyalty coalition businesses）。
2022 年 ICS 税前利润为 5.78 亿美元，上年为 9.29 亿美元；业绩显著受美元走强影响。
raw_excerpt: ICS issues a wide range of proprietary consumer, small business and corporate cards outside the United States. ICS also provides services to our international customers, including travel and lifestyle services, and manages certain international joint ventures and our loyalty coalition businesses.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — MD&A Business Environment (international billed business growth)
key_points: International billed business grew 23% year over year in 2022, or 36% on an FX-adjusted basis.
The international growth was attributed to a strong recovery in spend across both consumer and commercial customers.
Total revenues net of interest expense increased 25% year over year in 2022 (27% FX-adjusted).
Discount revenue, the largest revenue line, increased 25% year over year, driven primarily by Card Member spending volumes.
Net card fees increased 17% year over year; service fees and other revenues increased 36%; net interest income increased 28%.
The company reported 2022 net income of $7.5 billion, or $9.85 per share, versus $8.1 billion, or $10.02 per share, in 2021.

key_points: Amex operates a payments network with relationships with third-party banks and institutions in approximately 103 countries and territories.

For the year ended December 31, 2022, worldwide network services processed volume (spending on American Express cards issued by third parties) was $214.5 billion and at December 31, 2022, we had 56.5 million cards-in-force issued by third parties worldwide.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Item 1. Business: bank holding company status and segments (p.4)
key_points: American Express Company and its principal operating subsidiary, American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. (TRS), are bank holding companies under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the BHC Act).
As bank holding companies they are subject to supervision and examination by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.

The company reports four reportable operating segments: U.S. Consumer Services (USCS), Commercial Services (CS), International Card Services (ICS) and Global Merchant and Network Services (GMNS), plus Corporate & Other.
American Express Company was incorporated in 1965 as a New York corporation.
raw_excerpt:
We were founded in 1850 as a joint stock association and were incorporated in 1965 as a New York corporation. American Express Company and its principal operating subsidiary, American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. (TRS), are bank holding companies under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the BHC Act), subject to supervision and examination by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the Federal Reserve).
We principally engage in businesses comprising four reportable operating segments: U.S. Consumer Services (USCS), Commercial Services (CS), International Card Services (ICS) and Global Merchant and Network Services (GMNS).

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Note 22 Regulatory Matters and Capital Adequacy (p.150)
key_points: The company's U.S. bank subsidiary, American Express National Bank (AENB), is subject to supervision and regulation, including regulatory capital and leverage requirements, by the OCC.
American Express Company is supervised and regulated by the Federal Reserve and subject to its risk-based capital and leverage ratio requirements.
As of December 31, 2022 and 2021, the company and AENB met all capital requirements and maintained ratios in excess of those required to qualify as well capitalized.
At December 31, 2022, the aggregate amount of net assets of subsidiaries restricted from transfer was approximately $12.0 billion.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Deposit Programs / funding (p.68)
key_points: Deposits are offered within the U.S. bank subsidiary AENB and are FDIC-insured up to at least $250,000 per account holder.
AENB offers FDIC-insured high-yield savings accounts and certificates of deposit directly to consumers, and also offers checking account products.
As of December 31, 2022, the company had $110.2 billion in deposits.
The company had no commercial paper outstanding at any point during 2022.
raw_excerpt: We offer deposits within our U.S. bank subsidiary, AENB. These funds are currently insured up to an amount that is at least $250,000 per account holder through the FDIC. ... Direct retail deposits offered by AENB is our primary deposit product channel, which makes FDIC-insured high-yield savings account and certificates of deposit (CDs) products available directly to consumers. ... As of December 31, 2022, we had $110.2 billion in deposits.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Item 1. Business: Card Network Business (p.6)
key_points: The company operates a payments network through which it maintains relationships with third-party banks and other institutions in approximately 103 countries and territories, licensing the American Express brand.
Network partners are licensed to issue local-currency American Express-branded cards in their countries and/or serve as merchant acquirer for local merchants on the network.
For the year ended December 31, 2022, worldwide network services processed volume (spending on American Express cards issued by third parties) was $214.5 billion.
At December 31, 2022, there were 56.5 million cards-in-force issued by third parties worldwide.
raw_excerpt:
We operate a payments network through which we establish and maintain relationships with third-party banks and other institutions in approximately 103 countries and territories, licensing the American Express brand and extending the reach of our global network. These network partners are licensed to issue local currency American Express-branded cards in their countries and/or serve as the merchant acquirer for local merchants on our network.
For the year ended December 31, 2022, worldwide network services processed volume (spending on American Express cards issued by third parties) was $214.5 billion and at December 31, 2022, we had 56.5 million cards-in-force issued by third parties worldwide.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Note 23 Significant Credit Concentrations (p.152)
key_points: The geographic regions with the largest concentration outside the United States are the United Kingdom, Japan, the European Union, Australia, Canada and Mexico.

On-balance-sheet credit exposure to individuals was $156 billion in 2022 ($129 billion United States, $27 billion outside the United States) versus $131 billion in 2021 ($108 billion United States, $23 billion outside the United States).
Approximately 80 percent of the roughly $350 billion of unused credit at December 31, 2022 was related to customers within the United States.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Risk Factors: Russia/Belarus operations suspension (p.26)
key_points: Following the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the company announced that it suspended all business operations in Russia and Belarus.
The filing attributes to the conflict economic uncertainty and market disruptions, including heightened energy prices, and the imposition of financial and economic sanctions and export controls.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Business Environment (international billed business growth and FX headwind)
key_points: International billed business grew 23 percent year-over-year in 2022.
The strengthening U.S. dollar relative to the prior year against most major currencies had a negative impact on international billings.
U.S. Consumer billed business grew 24 percent year-over-year; Commercial Services billed business grew 21 percent year-over-year.
Worldwide network volumes increased 21 percent (24 percent FX-adjusted); billed business was 86 percent of total network volumes and increased 23 percent (25 percent FX-adjusted).
raw_excerpt: International billed business grew by 23 percent … continuing strengthening of the U.S. dollar, relative to the prior year, against most major currencies in which we operate, had a negative impact on our international billings.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — International Card Services (ICS) segment results, Table 13
key_points: ICS issues proprietary consumer, small business and corporate cards outside the United States, and manages certain international joint ventures and loyalty coalition businesses.
ICS 2022 total revenues net of interest expense were $9,061M, up 22 percent from $7,435M in 2021.
ICS 2022 pretax segment income was $578M versus $929M in 2021, a decline of 38 percent.
The 10-K attributes the ICS result decline to significant impact from the strengthening of the U.S. dollar.
ICS 2022 discount revenue rose 25 percent (37 percent FX-adjusted) on billed business growth of 23 percent (36 percent FX-adjusted); net card fees rose 3 percent (14 percent FX-adjusted).
raw_excerpt: ICS issues a wide range of proprietary consumer, small business and corporate cards outside the United States. ICS also provides services to our international customers, including travel and lifestyle services, and manages certain international joint ventures and our loyalty coalition businesses. … For 2022, ICS reported pretax income of $578 million, compared with $929 million a year ago. Results for this segment were significantly impacted by the strengthening of the U.S. dollar.
